# Second review: lessons, labs, and learning experience

Reviewed on 20 October 2026 by three independent audit passes covering curriculum, executable practice, and the learning portal, followed by integration checks. The review inspected all 24 lessons, eight labs, three capstones, assessment rules, and learner commands. Findings below distinguish repaired defects from further development.

## Highest-impact repairs

| Finding | Why it mattered | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Some incorrect student implementations passed their gates | A learner could receive misleading evidence of competence | Added negative and boundary checks for ordering, ticket-specific operation keys, retry inputs, replay events, citations, conflicting evidence, and escalation schemas |
| Rejected tool proposals could leak arbitrary input into traces | The reference contradicted its own logging guidance | Replaced raw proposal metadata with registry-defined labels and hashes; added regression checks using synthetic secret markers |
| Research capstone promised an absent source corpus | The project could not be attempted as described | Supplied eight synthetic sources, six questions, twelve claim-source labels, and a worked recommendation |
| Development lessons suggested defects already fixed in the reference | There was no reliable starting failure | Added an isolated budget-boundary defect with five checks and one expected initial failure |
| Stage and capstone requirements conflicted | Learners could follow one document and fail another | Standardized the capstone at 30/40 with every dimension at least 2; aligned all three routes, time estimates, and study schedule |
| No executable route from a chat-model answer to the harness | Most supplied practice demonstrated deterministic software only | Added a manual model-response bridge: export a prompt, save JSON, replay it through the real validator, tool permissions, storage, and evaluator |
| Solution links lost their target and long notes disappeared after reload | The portal could interrupt learning or lose work | Restored code downloads and section links, preserved long notes, and retained both versions of conflicting imported notes |

## Teaching and usability improvements

The new [practice map](PRACTICE-MAP.md) states prerequisites and connects each lesson to a concrete artifact or executable exercise. It explains that labs 01–07 are standalone helpers, while lab 08 integrates a decision policy. The [model bridge](../lab/model-bridge.md) provides a controlled comparison protocol and explicitly separates mock results from actual saved model answers.

Lesson 15 now assesses monetary-budget reasoning with reservation and reconciliation cases. Lesson 17 includes false-acceptance and false-rejection denominators. The assessment manual supplies score anchors and examples that fail despite a sufficient total. Quiz answer positions are balanced without changing the correct answers.

The portal now handles malformed routes, deduplicates progress records, supports keyboard progress import, and exposes the lab guides and research fixtures. Rebuilding an extracted source archive also recreates its downloadable ZIP.

## Follow-up: integration gaps closed

The three next-priority items from this review now have runnable follow-up labs:

| Earlier gap | Delivered follow-up | Evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real local MCP client/server | [Lab 09](../content/labs/09-real-mcp.md) | Official SDK, real subprocess transport, recorded requests/results and failure probes |
| Host-specific skill installation | [Lab 10](../content/labs/10-installed-skill.md) | Disposable project installation plus separate fresh-host behavioral checks |
| Composed student harness | [Lab 11](../content/labs/11-complete-student-harness.md) | All eight helpers invoked through declared seams, component identity and integration gates |

The [integration route](INTEGRATION-LABS.md) and [verification record](VERIFICATION.md) describe setup and observed results. The earlier paragraph about isolated helpers describes the original component exercises; lab 11 adds their operational composition without replacing the reference path.

Further development opportunities remain: a live provider transport and model-selected tool loop; more independently graded examples at every stage; and a learner pilot to measure completion times, exercise clarity and teaching effectiveness. These were not the three integration deliverables requested in the follow-up. The bridge still replays one saved decision, and neither deterministic results nor a single host session proves future model reliability.

## Verification and limits

See the [verification record](VERIFICATION.md) for commands, test counts, browser checks, and the regenerated PDF. Automated checks cover the included cases; they cannot establish teaching effectiveness for every learner or justify a commercial price.

The intentionally broken development fixture must fail before repair. Unimplemented student functions must also fail their relevant practice checks. Neither is a defect in the passing reference implementation.
